beltLipo.heroSubtitle: Circumferential Body Contouring for Excess Skin
beltLipo.heroDesc1: Massive weight loss changes physiology faster than skin can adapt. When weight reduction is large or rapid, the abdominal and lower-back skin often loses its elastic recoil, creating a circumferential "apron" that wraps around the waist. This is not just a cosmetic issue. Patients commonly experience skin infections, difficulty with movement, poor clothing fit, and persistent discomfort despite achieving a healthy body weight.
beltLipo.heroDesc2: A belt lipectomy is a specialised body contouring surgery designed to remove this 360-degree excess skin and fat around the abdomen, waist, flanks, and lower back. In Malaysia, it is classified as a major surgical procedure and must be performed by a registered medical practitioner in a licensed medical facility under standards regulated by the Ministry of Health Malaysia (MOH).
beltLipo.heroDesc3: Unlike limited abdominal procedures, belt lipectomy restores balance to the entire lower torso, improving contour, posture, hygiene, and overall quality of life.
beltLipo.whatDesc1: A belt lipectomy is a circumferential excisional surgery that removes redundant skin and fat in a continuous "belt-like" pattern around the lower trunk. The incision typically extends around the waistline, allowing simultaneous correction of the abdomen, waist and flanks, lower back, and upper buttock contour.
beltLipo.whatDesc2: Major medical institutions describe circumferential body contouring as an effective reconstructive option for post–massive weight loss patients whose skin laxity cannot be corrected by exercise or diet alone.
beltLipo.whatNotPoint: Not a weight-loss surgery – it reshapes after weight has stabilised
beltLipo.whatYesPoint: Yes – it improves contour, posture, hygiene, and quality of life
beltLipo.whyTitle: Why Belt Lipectomy Is Different from a Tummy Tuck
beltLipo.whyDesc: A common misconception is that a tummy tuck can replace a belt lipectomy. Anatomically, they address different problems.
beltLipo.tummyDesc: Treats only the front of the abdomen
beltLipo.beltDesc: Treats the entire circumference of the lower torso
beltLipo.whyDesc2: Patients who have lost a large amount of weight often have excess skin not only in front, but also along the sides and lower back. Treating one area while leaving the rest uncorrected can lead to imbalance and suboptimal results.
beltLipo.areasDesc: By tightening tissues circumferentially, the procedure often improves buttock contour without implants.
beltLipo.processMainTitle: How Belt Lipectomy Surgery Is Performed
beltLipo.processMainDesc: Belt lipectomy is performed in a hospital setting under general anaesthesia. Because blood supply must be preserved across a long incision, the operation requires advanced surgical planning and experience.
beltLipo.benefitsDesc: For many patients, this surgery marks the final step in their weight-loss transformation.
beltLipo.benefit1Desc: Remove excess skin from entire lower torso
beltLipo.benefit3Desc: Elimination of chronic infections and rashes
beltLipo.candidateTitle: Who Typically Needs a Belt Lipectomy?
beltLipo.candidateDesc: Belt lipectomy is most suitable for patients who meet specific criteria to ensure safe and effective results.
beltLipo.candidate1: Have undergone massive weight loss (bariatric surgery or lifestyle change)
beltLipo.candidate2: Have maintained a stable weight for several months
beltLipo.candidate3: Experience circumferential skin laxity around the waist
beltLipo.candidate4: Suffer from rashes, hygiene issues, or functional limitation
beltLipo.candidate5: Are medically fit for major surgery
beltLipo.floatingBadgeDesc: Every belt lipectomy is personally performed by Dr. Soma with hospital-grade safety protocols.
beltLipo.compareTitle: Belt Lipectomy vs Lower Body Lift
beltLipo.compareDesc: While often used interchangeably, these procedures have subtle differences. The choice depends on skin laxity distribution, anatomy, and patient goals.
beltLipo.recoveryDesc: Healing follows predictable physiological phases when postoperative care is followed carefully.

beltLipo.faq1A: A circumferential surgery that removes excess skin and fat around the waist, abdomen, and lower back.
beltLipo.faq2A: When performed by a qualified plastic surgeon in a licensed hospital, it is a well-established and safe procedure.
beltLipo.faq3A: Initial recovery takes 2–3 weeks, with continued healing over several months.
beltLipo.faq4A: Yes. Scars are unavoidable but placed strategically and tend to fade with time.
beltLipo.faq5A: Postoperative discomfort is expected but usually controlled with medication.
beltLipo.faq6A: Results are long-lasting if body weight remains stable.
beltLipo.faq7A: Patients with unstable weight, uncontrolled medical illness, or unrealistic expectations.
beltLipo.safetyDesc: In Malaysia, belt lipectomy falls under private healthcare services regulated by the Ministry of Health Malaysia.
beltLipo.safety1Desc: Surgical facilities must be licensed, and surgeons must be fully registered and credentialed.
beltLipo.safety2Desc: Circumferential body contouring should be performed by trained specialists due to its complexity.
beltLipo.safety3Desc: All procedures performed in licensed hospital settings with full monitoring and sterile environments.
beltLipo.ctaDesc1: A belt lipectomy is not about aesthetics alone. It is a reconstructive procedure that restores comfort, movement, and proportion after massive weight loss.
beltLipo.ctaDesc2: When performed under regulated medical standards in Malaysia, it offers durable, life-changing results for the right candidate. A successful outcome depends on proper patient selection, experienced surgical hands, and disciplined postoperative care.
